title: Raft: elect a leader and commit an entry
description: A five-node Raft cluster has lost its leader. Elect a new one and commit the next payment config change.

problemStatement.overview:
payment-handler keeps its configuration in a five-node Raft cluster, the same algorithm behind etcd and Consul. The leader just crashed.

Raft gets the remaining nodes to agree on a single new leader for a new term, and then on the exact order of log entries. Everything rests on majorities: with five nodes, three is a majority, and any two majorities share at least one node.

The outline runs from the election timeout to the client getting its reply. Fill the blocks. Traps break safety or stall the cluster.
problemStatement.yourTask: Order the steps from a follower noticing the missing leader to a committed, applied log entry.
yourTaskSteps: Fill each empty block from Unused.
hints: Terms act as a logical clock. Higher terms win.
A vote is only granted to a candidate whose log is at least as up to date.
Committed means stored on a majority, not just on the leader.
problemStatement.moat:
Setter notes, not shown to learners.

Required chain: election-timeout → become-candidate → win-majority → leader-append → majority-replicated → apply-reply.
Optional splice: split-vote on become-candidate → win-majority.
Five traps.

platformSpec.passMessage: New term, majority vote, majority replication, then apply. That's Raft.

pieces.title: Election timeout fires
pieces.blurb: A follower hears no heartbeat before its randomized timeout (for example 150 to 300 ms) expires.

pieces.title: Become a candidate in a new term
pieces.blurb: It increments its term, votes for itself, and sends RequestVote to every other node.

pieces.title: Split vote, then retry
pieces.blurb: If two candidates split the votes and nobody reaches a majority, each waits a new random timeout and starts another term.

pieces.title: Win votes from a majority
pieces.blurb: Three of five nodes grant their vote. Each votes at most once per term, and only if the candidate's log is at least as up to date as its own.

pieces.title: Leader appends the entry and replicates
pieces.blurb: The new leader appends the client's config change to its log and sends AppendEntries to the followers.

pieces.title: Entry stored on a majority: committed
pieces.blurb: Once the entry is in the logs of three of five nodes, the leader advances its commit index.

pieces.title: Apply to the state machine and reply
pieces.blurb: The leader applies the entry and answers the client. Followers apply it when they learn the new commit index.

pieces.title: Every node uses the same fixed timeout
pieces.blurb: All followers wait exactly 200 ms, so the cluster reacts at a predictable moment.
pieces.trapIfPlaced: Identical timeouts make every node stand at once, so votes keep splitting. Raft randomizes them.

pieces.title: Win with votes from half the cluster
pieces.blurb: Half the nodes is enough to lead. In a four-node cluster, your own vote plus one more makes you leader.
pieces.trapIfPlaced: Raft needs a strict majority. Half is not enough, otherwise two leaders could win the same term.

pieces.title: Commit once the leader's disk has it
pieces.blurb: As soon as the leader fsyncs the entry locally, it is committed.
pieces.trapIfPlaced: If that leader crashes, a new leader without the entry could be elected. Commit needs a majority.

pieces.title: Accept entries from a lower term
pieces.blurb: A follower accepts AppendEntries from any node that claims to be leader, regardless of its term.
pieces.trapIfPlaced: Requests from an older term are rejected. That is how a deposed leader is stopped.

pieces.title: New leader deletes entries to match followers
pieces.blurb: If followers are missing entries, the leader removes those entries from its own log to agree with them.
pieces.trapIfPlaced: A Raft leader never overwrites or deletes its own log. Followers are brought in line with the leader.
